punchline: Seneca jumped into the sea in his cloak, then wrote that only the man who is awake can tell his dream.
thirty_sec: In Letter 53 Seneca sets out across the bay on a calm sea, ends up seasick, orders the pilot ashore and lowers himself into the water in his cloak; afterwards he notes that we hide even bodily faults, and mental ones best of all.
question: Which mistake of yours keeps coming back under a comfortable label?
key_contrast: Whoever can confess a fault is awake; the sound sleeper cannot tell his dream.
